evidence.description: The authentication handler registers a visit or resets seeds, but does not synchronize authentication or profile properties; authStateLoaded does nothing.
Authentication and profile properties are synchronized in the separate profile-update handler, with isLoggedIn additionally deferred to a task.
Seed refresh behavior depends on the potentially stale isLoggedIn property.

candidates.explanation: The authentication-state observer never updates isLoggedIn, userProfile, username, or avatarURL. After initialization, these values are synchronized only by a separate profile-update notification, and even that handler defers isLoggedIn to another task. Consequently, authentication notifications alone leave the published authentication state stale, while refreshSeedState and seed-progress handling continue to branch on that stale value.
candidates.title: Authentication changes do not synchronize published auth state

evidence.description: Untracked tasks capture a token and apply success or failure state after awaiting the request without checking whether the session or request is still current.
Responses overwrite level, progress, and balance without validating their association with the current state.
Logout resets local seed and level state but does not invalidate outstanding visit requests.

candidates.explanation: Each visit registration starts an independent task and unconditionally applies its response after the network suspension. There is no cancellation, session validation, or request-order check. A response from before logout can overwrite the locally reset balance and level, and overlapping refreshes can apply responses out of order. A late failure can likewise publish an error for a session that has already ended.
candidates.title: In-flight visit requests can overwrite newer session state

evidence.description: The delayed callbacks write a captured balance and later clear the shared increment without any validity or ownership check.
New balance responses can either schedule another animation or immediately replace the balance while previous callbacks remain pending.
The logout reset changes the balance without invalidating pending animation callbacks.

candidates.explanation: Every balance animation schedules unconditional future writes to seedCount and balanceIncrement. These callbacks are neither canceled nor checked against subsequent balance changes or logout. An older scheduled animation can therefore overwrite a newer balance or a logout reset, and an earlier animation's cleanup can clear the increment belonging to a later animation.
candidates.title: Delayed animation callbacks can apply stale balance state

evidence.description: The nonisolated shared property initializes the provider inside MainActor.assumeIsolated without ensuring main-actor execution.

candidates.explanation: The shared property is explicitly nonisolated, so first access is permitted outside the main actor. Its lazy initializer nevertheless uses MainActor.assumeIsolated, which checks isolation rather than dispatching to the main actor. First access from another executor can therefore fail the isolation assertion instead of creating the singleton.
candidates.title: Nonisolated singleton initialization assumes main-actor execution
